subject: Dedicated GPU fleet sizing & SLO fit for Aurora Health PoC
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha.p@aurorahealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PoC sizing ask - expected load and SLOs

Laura —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. We want to lock down dedicated sizing for the 6-week PoC so procurement can provision budget. A few concrete numbers from our side:
- Production-like peak: 30 requests/sec (RPS) during business hours, with short bursts to 60 RPS for 90s during batch window.
- Average request payload: ~1,100 tokens (many are long-document summarizations + extraction).
- Target SLO: 95th-percentile end-to-end response latency <= 750ms for complete generation. If we can hit 500–600ms even better.
- Model profile: prefer a transformer with 8k context; we care about coherence for ~1k tokens output.

Can you provide a per-GPU tokens/sec estimate you intend to size to, the resulting GPU count for steady-state and burst headroom, and any cache/batching optimizations that would reduce committed capacity? We also need a short writeup to attach to our purchase request.

I've attached a procurement template (procurement_PO_template.pdf will follow from procurement@aurorahealth.com).

Best,
Asha
CTO, Aurora Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.p@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PoC sizing ask - expected load and SLOs

Asha —

Thanks for the clear numbers. Attached is a first-pass calculation (aurora_capacity_calc_v1.xlsx) and a short SLO summary (aurora_slo_summary.pdf). High-level conclusions up front:

1) Baseline tokens/sec math (steady-state):
   - Steady RPS: 30 RPS * 1,100 tokens/request = 33,000 tokens/sec required.
   - We assume model variant: rw-13b-8bit-optimized (quantized kernels) with observed throughput ~820 tokens/sec per A100-style GPU for long-form generation at the requested output lengths (this is our conservative number including KV cache/attention overhead).
   - GPUs needed (no headroom): ceil(33,000 / 820) = 41 GPUs.

2) Burst headroom and safety margin:
   - Burst to 60 RPS -> 66,000 tokens/sec -> baseline GPUs = 81.
   - Typical practice: reserve 1.5x steady-state headroom for safe tail-SLO and unplanned spikes -> 41 * 1.5 = 62 GPUs.
   - Alternatively, we can provision 41 dedicated GPUs + a shared burst pool of 25 GPUs (on-demand/backfill) to cover spikes to 60 RPS while keeping committed footprint lower.

3) Caching and batching impact:
   - If you can cache ~25% of prefix tokens (document re-use across requests) we reduce tokens/sec to ~24,750 -> GPUs -> ceil(24,750/820) = 31 GPUs steady-state.
   - Workload-aware batching for short requests can further improve tokens/sec effective throughput by ~10–20% for mixed loads; this is workload dependent.

4) Latency vs. CPU/GPU selection:
   - The 820 tokens/sec number maps to median per-token latency ~1.2ms token; end-to-end for 1,100 tokens at median would be ~1.3s which exceeds your 750ms SLO. To meet 750ms for full generation we need faster per-GPU throughput or sharding across GPUs (model parallelism).
   - Options: pick a 34B quantized variant on multi-GPU sharded instances to reduce end-to-end latency (but increases committed GPUs and cost), or accept partial streaming (stream earlier tokens) to meet SLO for first-token latency while the remainder streams.

Next steps: Marcus, can you confirm the 820 tokens/sec figure on our validated kernel data for rw-13b-8bit on A100 and provide an alternate plan with sharded inference numbers? Also whether burst pool via Dedicated + Hosted fallback is the recommended commercial setup for Aurora.

Asha — I'll follow up with a one-page procurement-friendly summary you can attach.

Thanks,
Laura
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Asha Patel <asha.p@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-05T08:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PoC sizing ask - expected load and SLOs

Laura / Asha —

Confirmed on the performance baseline: 820 tokens/sec per A100-class GPU is conservative for rw-13b-8bit with our latest fused attention and KV-cache paths when the full 8k context is used and outputs approach ~1k tokens. Benchmarks (internal run ID: perf-202605) show median token generation ~1.1ms/token and 95th token latency bump under heavy contention.

Sharded path (lower latency):
- 2-way tensor-parallel sharding on 2x A100 VMs gives roughly 1.9x aggregate tokens/sec (so ~1,560 tokens/sec effective for single-request throughput). For the customer's 1,100 tokens, end-to-end median moves to ~700ms (fits the 750ms SLO), 95th ~900ms without additional headroom.
- GPUs needed steady-state (sharded): ceil(33,000 / 1,560) = 22 GPUs (11 two-way shards); add 1.25x safety -> 28 GPUs committed.

Cost/operational note: sharded instances increase networking/slots complexity and per-deployment initialization time; however, for latency-sensitive customers they are the recommended path.

Recommended commercial configuration for Aurora PoC:
- Commit: 30 dedicated GPUs (2-way sharded configuration yielding ~1,560 tokens/sec per shard pair) to meet SLO with modest safety margin.
- Burst pool: ability to burst to an additional 15 GPUs from Redwood Hosted for short spikes (90–120s).
- Caching: enable prefix KV caching on stable document identifiers (we expect ~20–25% token reduction for typical Aurora reuse patterns).
- Rolling canary: start PoC on 10 committed GPUs for first 2 weeks (validate effective tokens/sec and cache hit rates) then ramp to 30 if metrics align.

I've added an alternate sheet in the attached calc with 2-way sharded math and the canary plan.

—Marcus
Engineering, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

From: Asha Patel <asha.p@aurorahealth.com>

Laura / Marcus —

Appreciate the detailed math and options. Procurement wants a short commitment to justify a 12% PoC discount. Our preference: 30 dedicated GPUs (2-way sharded pairs) with the hosted burst pool as you suggested, and a 3-month paid PoC term. Please prepare a one-page statement of work with the following included: committed GPUs, burst policy, expected steady-state latency numbers, and acceptance criteria (cache hit >= 18% and 95th percentile response <= 900ms).

If you can send a DocuSign with the commercial terms and a short setup checklist we can get internal approvals this week.

Asha
CTO, Aurora Health
